gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the BLUETTI Apex 300's built-in solar ports accept only 12–60 V and 20 A per port. BLUETTI's own SORA 500 panels (49.1 V Voc) can't be wired in series on them, so the store's 'Apex 300 + 2 × 500W' bundle tops out at 1,000 W. Reaching 2,000 W or more takes the $699 SolarX 4K and at least four SORA 500s in series, because three in series give 147.3 V, under its 150 V minimum.
standout_why: EnergySage (cited) lists the Apex 300 at '2,400 W (more with SolarX 4K)'. On panels it only says to 'stay within the unit's voltage and wattage limits' and gives no voltage window, Voc rule or panel count. Solar Waypoint (cited) gives voltage ranges for the F3800 Plus (11–165 V) and DELTA Pro Ultra (80–450 V) but nothing for the Apex 300, and has no series/parallel or Voc guidance. ChatGPT's own answer told the shopper 'Apex 300 … 2,400 W solar input' with no caveat. thiswatt.com (cited) would not load because of a TLS certificate error, so it is not checked. The finding decides the set: it decides whether the cart needs the SolarX 4K and how many panels the cart needs.
kit_items: power station: BLUETTI Apex 300 (2,764.8 Wh, 3,840 W, 120/240 V from one unit per StorageReview). It is the BLUETTI pick ChatGPT showed, and it's in stock on bluettipower.com.

high-voltage solar controller: BLUETTI SolarX 4K (150–500 V panel input, up to 4 kW, steps down to below 60 V for the Apex 300). Without it the built-in 12–60 V ports can't take a series string. One store SKU bundles it with the Apex 300.

panels: 4 × BLUETTI SORA 500 (49.1 V Voc, 40.92 V Vmp, 12.22 A Imp, MC4) wired in series into the SolarX 4K. That gives 196.4 V Voc, which clears the 150 V minimum, and about 2,000 W (163.7 V × 12.22 A). Three in series (147.3 V) falls short of the minimum.

wiring: a PV disconnect switch between the string and the SolarX 4K. Notebookcheck says it must be bought separately, and I found none on bluettipower.com. Add BLUETTI MC4 extension cables ($59, 30 A) to reach the array.

BLUETTI Solar Extension Cable (MC4, 5 m / 10 m, 30 A) | https://www.bluettipower.com/products/bluetti-solar-extension-cable | $59.00 | 2026-11-13

findings.label: built-in solar input
findings.note: From the reviewer's spec table. 1,200 W per port = 60 V × 20 A, which is the top of the voltage window. A panel string only runs below its Voc, so the real per-port ceiling is the panel's Vmp × 20 A. The maker's US manual PDF (s4.bluettipower.com) was over 10 MB and could not be opened.

findings.label: charging temperature
findings.note: An off-grid unit kept in an unheated shed won't take a solar charge below freezing.

findings.label: 240 V output
findings.value: 240 V from a single unit (NEMA 14-50R, 50 A)
findings.note: Not a trap: unlike earlier BLUETTI units, it needs no second station or bridging cable, per the reviewer.

findings.label: electrical specs
findings.value: Voc 49.1 V, Vmp 40.92 V, Imp 12.22 A, Isc 13.31 A, MC4
findings.source_title: The Bluetti Sora 500 Solar Panel Review (Andrew Paul, Impulse Gamer, 2026-08-02)
findings.note: Andrew Paul measured about 400 W average on an Elite 300 in Australian winter. Arithmetic on the Apex 300 built-in ports: 2 in series = 98.2 V Voc, over the 60 V limit, so series is not allowed. One per port = 40.92 × 12.22 = 500 W, so the 'Apex 300 + 2 × 500W' bundle gives 1,000 W at most. Two in parallel per port = 24.44 A Imp, capped at 20 A, about 818 W per port, so 4 panels give about 1,637 W, not 2,400 W. BLUETTI's US/EU/AU panel pages would not load (redirect loop or HTTP 429).

findings.label: panel voltage window and price
findings.value: 150–500 V panel input, up to 4 kW, steps down to below 60 V; $699.00
findings.source_title: SolarX 4K & Locking Terminal to P090D Adapter Cable (for Single Use) – BLUETTI US
findings.note: Store text via storecheck. Lists Apex 300 as compatible. With SORA 500s: 3 in series = 147.3 V, below the 150 V minimum. 4 in series = 196.4 V Voc and 163.7 V Vmp, so 163.7 × 12.22 ≈ 2,000 W. Notebookcheck's spec table gives 120–500 V Voc (MPPT 120–450 V), but the BLUETTI store says 150 V, so I size to 150 V. The separate '…to XT60 Adapter Cable (for Parallel Use)' SKU is also $699 and is the one for multiple Apex 300 units.

findings.value: PV switch must be bought separately; panels ≤20 A
findings.source_title: First look at the Bluetti SolarX 4K (Christian Hintze, Notebookcheck, 2025-10-06, updated 2026-11-01)
findings.note: Connects to the Apex 300 by a P090A DC cable plus a LAN cable. Hintze reports the Apex 300 reached up to 4,000 W of solar with the SolarX 4K, against a 2,400 W limit without it. A storecheck search for 'PV switch' on bluettipower.com returned none.
